description: Granite is a coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock composed mostly of quartz, alkali feldspar, and plagioclase.
common_location: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve, Pandan area, Pulau Ubin, Sembawang
fun_fact: Pulau Ubin once had multiple granite quarries that supplied building material for many early structures in Singapore, including the Istana and Raffles Lighthouse.

description: Sandstone is a clastic sedimentary rock composed mainly of sand-sized mineral particles or rock fragments.
color: tan, yellow, red, brown, gray, or white
common_location: Jurong East, Tuas, Clementi, Pasir Panjang
fun_fact: The Jurong Formation in Singapore includes sandstone, siltstone, and shale—and is around 200 million years old!

description: Mudstone is a fine-grained sedimentary rock formed from ancient mud—a mix of clay and silt-sized particles
fun_fact: Mudstone in the Jurong Formation may contain fossilized plant material, offering clues to the tropical environment of ancient Singapore over 200 million years ago!

description: Limestone is a sedimentary rock primarily composed of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), often formed from the accumulated remains of marine organisms like coral and shellfish
common_location: Pulau Ubin, Pandan, Pasir Panjang, Jurong Island
fun_fact: Singapore has limited natural limestone compared to granie or sandstone, so if you found it, consider yourself lucky!

description: Quartzite is a hard, non-foliated metamorphic rock that was originally pure quartz sandstone.
color: White, Gray, Yellow, Green, Blue and Orange
common_location: Pulao Tekong, Pulao Sajahat, Punggol Point
fun_fact: stone tools made from quartzite have been found at archaeological sites, including Tanjong Karang (now Tuas) and Pulau Ubin, suggesting its use by early inhabitants.

description: Gabbro is a coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock that forms from the slow cooling of magma beneath the Earth's surface.
fun_fact: Gabbro makes up much of the Earth’s oceanic crust and is the intrusive equivalent of basalt. When polished, it is sometimes sold as "Black Granite" in the construction industry—even though it’s a different rock!

description: Basalt is a dark-colored, fine-grained igneous rock that forms from the rapid cooling of low-silica lava at or near the Earth’s surface.
fun_fact: Basalt covers most of the ocean floor and is also found on the Moon and Mars!

description: Andesite is a fine-grained volcanic rock formed from the eruption of magma with intermediate silica content.
common_location: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve, Mandai, Sembawang
fun_fact: In Singapore, although surface volcanic activity doesn't exist, andesite dykes provide evidence of ancient volcanic processes deep underground!

description: Amphibolite is a dark, dense metamorphic rock mainly composed of amphibole minerals (usually hornblende) and plagioclase feldspar.
fun_fact: Amphibolite is so durable that it has been used for grinding stones and construction for centuries.

description: Marble is a metamorphic rock that forms when limestone is subjected to high pressure and temperature, causing its calcite crystals to recrystallize.
composition: Calcium carbonate, Mica, Quartz, Graphite, Iron Oxides
common_location: (not found naturally) Flooring, Wall cladding, countertops
fun_fact: Despite being soft, marble was the stone of choice for Michelangelo, who sculpted the famous Statue of David entirely from Carrara marble.

description: Schist is a medium- to high-grade metamorphic rock characterized by its pronounced foliation, meaning it has easily visible layers or plates of minerals.
composition:
Mica minerals (biotite, muscovite)
commonly contains quartz, feldspar, chlorite, garnet, staurolite, kyanite
common_location: Murai Area in Northwest of Singapore
fun_fact: The term “schist” comes from the Greek word skhistos, meaning “split.”

description: Norite is a coarse-grained mafic intrusive igneous rock that is similar to gabbro but contains orthopyroxene instead of clinopyroxene as its dominant dark mineral.
fun_fact: Norite is found on the Moon and in Martian meteorites!

description: Argillite is a hardened, compacted sedimentary rock derived from mudstone or shale.
fun_fact: Argillite can become slate under higher-grade metamorphism. In some places, it was historically used by Indigenous peoples (e.g., in Canada) for carving ceremonial objects

description: Siltstone is a fine-grained sedimentary rock composed primarily of silt-sized particles that are finer than sand but coarser than clay.
fun_fact: Although not as well-known as sandstone or shale, siltstone often records ancient environments

description: Conglomerate is a coarse-grained clastic sedimentary rock made up of rounded fragments (called clasts) that are greater than 2 mm in diameter, cemented together by finer materials like sand, silt, or clay.
composition:
Clasts: Rounded fragments of quartz, chert, granite, or other rocks
Matrix:  Fine particles like sand, silt, or clay
Cemented by silica, calcite, or iron oxide
fun_fact: Conglomerates are like "natural concrete", often preserving a record of ancient river systems or shoreline environments.

description: Chert is a hard, fine-grained sedimentary rock composed mostly of microcrystalline quartz
common_location: Small nodules or layers within Jurong Formation sedimentary rocks
fun_fact: Chert was widely used by prehistoric humans to make tools and weapons because it breaks with sharp edges.

description: Granulite is a high-grade metamorphic rock that forms under extreme temperature and pressure, typically deep in the continental crust.
fun_fact: Granulite represents some of the deepest and most ancient parts of Earth's crust.

description: Gneiss is a high-grade metamorphic rock characterized by its distinctive banded or foliated appearance, formed under intense pressure and temperature.
fun_fact: The word "gneiss" comes from the German word meaning "spark," possibly referring to its shiny mineral layers.

description: Carbonatite is a rare igneous rock composed of more than 50% carbonate minerals, unlike typical igneous rocks which are silicate-based.
composition: Calcite, dolomite, ankerite, apatite, magnetite, barite
fun_fact: Carbonatites are economically significant because they often contain rare earth elements (REEs), niobium, and phosphates, materials that are critical for making electronics, magnets, and green technologies.

description: Granitoids are a broad family of coarse-grained intrusive igneous rocks that are compositionally similar to granite.
composition: Quartz, feldspar, micas, silica, alkali and calcium content
common_location: Central Singapore, Bukit Timah, Mandai, Sembawang
fun_fact: Granitoids form the foundation of many continental crusts and are often associated with mountain-building and plate tectonic activity.

description: Diamictite is a coarse-grained, clastic sedimentary rock composed of a wide range of grain sizes, from clay to boulders, all embedded in a finer-grained matrix.
composition: heterogeneous mix of clasts (pebbles, cobbles, boulders
fun_fact: Diamictite is the lithified equivalent of glacial till and may contain dropstones — large clasts dropped into fine sediment by melting icebergs.

description: Breccia is a coarse-grained clastic rock composed of angular rock fragments (called clasts) that are cemented together by a finer-grained matrix.
composition:
Angular clasts: made of various rocks (e.g., limestone, granite, basalt)
Matrix may consist of clay, silt, sand, or calcite
Cementing agents often include silica, calcite, or iron oxides
common_location: Jurong Formation, fault zones, weathered outcrops
fun_fact: The word "breccia" comes from the Italian word for "broken stones."

description: Anthracite is the highest rank of coal, formed through the metamorphism of bituminous coal.
color: Jet black with a metallic to submetallic sheen
fun_fact: Due to its high carbon purity and clean-burning properties, anthracite was historically used for home heating, especially in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

description: Blueschist is a rare, high-pressure, low-temperature metamorphic rock that forms in subduction zones, where oceanic crust is forced deep into the Earth’s mantle.
fun_fact: Blueschist forms at depths of 15–30 km in subduction zones but at relatively low temperatures (200–500°C).

description: Chalk is a soft, white to light-gray, fine-grained sedimentary rock made almost entirely of the microscopic shells of marine organisms like coccolithophores.
composition: calcium carbonate, clay, quartz, organic matter
fun_fact: Chalk is so porous and pure that it can store and filter water—it forms important aquifers in Europe.

description: Coal is a carbon-rich, combustible sedimentary rock formed from the remains of plants that accumulated in swampy environments millions of years ago.
color: black, dark brown with dull to shiny luster
composition:
Mostly carbon (C) (up to 90% in anthracite)

Also contains hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, and moisture

May contain inorganic minerals like clay, quartz, pyrite
fun_fact: Coal has been used as a fuel source for over 3,000 years, but today it's also crucial in producing steel, cement, and even carbon fiber materials.

description: Dolomite is a sedimentary carbonate rock primarily composed of the mineral dolomite.
color: white, light gray, pink, tan, or buff
composition:
Predominantly dolomite mineral (CaMg(CO₃)₂)

May contain calcite, quartz, clay, or organic matter
fun_fact: The Dolomite mineral and rock are named after the French geologist Déodat Gratet de Dolomieu, who first described the rock in the 18th century.

description: Eclogite is a dense, coarse-grained metamorphic rock that forms under extremely high-pressure and high-temperature conditions, typically in subduction zones where oceanic crust is driven deep into the Earth’s mantle.
color: Dark green to black groundmass with visible red or pink garnet crystals
composition:
Primarily omphacite (a type of pyroxene, greenish)

Garnet (pyrope-almandine series, reddish)

No plagioclase, which is a key diagnostic feature
fun_fact: Eclogite forms at depths of over 40–60 km and may contain coesite, a high-pressure form of quartz, indicating ultrahigh-pressure metamorphism.

description: Evaporites are a group of sedimentary rocks formed by the evaporation of water, usually in closed basins such as lakes, inland seas, or tidal flats.
color: white, gray, colorless, or pale yellow
composition:
Composed of evaporite minerals, including:

Halite (NaCl)

Gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O)

Anhydrite (CaSO₄)

Sylvite (KCl)

Borates, nitrates, and carbonates in smaller amounts
density:
Halite: ~2.1–2.2 g/cm³

Gypsum: ~2.3 g/cm³

Anhydrite: ~2.9 g/cm³
fun_fact: Evaporites such as halite (rock salt) have been mined and used for thousands of years—not only for preserving food but also for de-icing roads, manufacturing, and geological storage of gases (like CO₂ and natural gas) due to their impermeability.

description: Flint is a hard, microcrystalline form of quartz (silica) that occurs as nodules or layers within chalk or limestone formations.
color: dark gray, black, or brown with a waxy or glassy luster
composition: silica (SiO₂) in the form of microcrystalline quartz (cryptocrystalline quartz)
fun_fact: Flint was used extensively in prehistoric times to make tools and weapons because it fractures conchoidally, forming sharp edges.

description: Low-grade metamorphic rock with green minerals like chlorite and actinolite.
fun_fact: Named for its green minerals and schistose texture.

description: Dark, coarse-grained sandstone with a mix of rock fragments and matrix.
fun_fact: Often forms in tectonically active deep marine environments.

description: Hard, fine-grained rock formed by contact metamorphism.
fun_fact: Name comes from its horn-like toughness.

description: Rare volcanic rock rich in magnesium, formed in early Earth history.
fun_fact: Only forms at very high temperatures; largely Archean in age.

description: Rock that has undergone partial melting, mix of igneous and metamorphic textures.
fun_fact: Often forms at the transition between metamorphism and melting.

description: Volcanic glass formed from rapidly cooled lava.
fun_fact: Breaks with sharp edges; used by ancient civilizations for tools and weapons.

description: Fine-grained sedimentary rock containing kerogen.
fun_fact: Can be heated to produce synthetic oil (shale oil).

description: Limestone made of ooids—tiny spherical grains formed by concentric precipitation of calcium carbonate.
fun_fact: Named after the Greek word for egg, 'oon', due to its rounded grains.

description: Very coarse-grained igneous rock, often granitic in composition.
fun_fact: Known for containing rare minerals and large crystals.

description: Fine-grained metamorphic rock with a satiny sheen and slight foliation.
fun_fact: Forms from the metamorphism of slate and grades into schist.

description: Rock with large crystals (phenocrysts) in a fine-grained groundmass.
fun_fact: Important in ore deposits—often hosts copper and gold.

description: Lightweight, vesicular volcanic rock that can float on water.
fun_fact: Formed from explosive volcanic eruptions; used in abrasives.

description: Dense igneous rock composed mainly of pyroxene minerals.
fun_fact: Often found in mantle-derived rocks; can contain valuable minerals.

description: Intermediate intrusive rock with more quartz than diorite.
fun_fact: Similar to granite but with less quartz and more dark minerals.

description: Granitoid rock with roughly equal plagioclase and orthoclase feldspar.
fun_fact: Often used as decorative stone or building material.

description: Nearly pure quartz igneous rock with very little feldspar or other minerals.
fun_fact: Rare rock that is almost entirely quartz.

description: Fine-grained, silica-rich volcanic rock, equivalent to granite.
fun_fact: Often associated with explosive volcanic eruptions.

description: Dark-colored, vesicular volcanic rock, heavier and denser than pumice.
fun_fact: Commonly used as landscaping material and in barbecue grills.

description: Rock composed largely of serpentine group minerals, formed by hydration of ultramafic rocks.
fun_fact: May contain asbestos; has a slippery, soapy feel.

description: Fine-grained sedimentary rock formed from compacted mud and clay.
fun_fact: Source rock for oil and gas in many basins.

description: Fine-grained foliated metamorphic rock derived from shale.
fun_fact: Splits easily into flat sheets; used for roofing and tiles.

description: Rock composed of talc and carbonate minerals, often forming from ultramafic rocks.
fun_fact: Very soft; can be used in talcum powder and as a carving stone.

description: Fine-grained volcanic rock with feldspathoid minerals and little quartz.
fun_fact: Found in volcanic provinces with alkali-rich magmas.

description: Limestone formed by the precipitation of calcium carbonate from mineral springs.
fun_fact: Often forms beautiful terraces and is used as a decorative stone.

description: Rock formed from compacted volcanic ash and debris from explosive eruptions.
fun_fact: Used as a lightweight building stone since ancient times.

description: Deposits from turbidity currents, showing graded bedding from underwater landslides.
fun_fact: Important indicators of deep marine sedimentary processes.

description: Mud-supported carbonate rock with more than 10% grains.
fun_fact: Part of the Dunham classification for limestones.

description: Rock that has undergone strong deformation, showing foliation, lineation, or other tectonic structures.
fun_fact: Records the deformation history of rocks during tectonic events.

description: Rock formed by chemical exchange between magma and carbonate rocks near a contact zone.
fun_fact: Often hosts economically valuable minerals like tungsten, copper, and iron.
